$comment: Rule catalog — ensemble. Standards 10 and 11: model disagreement and ensemble behavior. Carries two prohibitions: ignoring major disagreement, and cherry-picking models. Every rule here applies only to predictions; an abstention has no ensemble output to describe.

rules.title: Ensemble members are named and versioned
rules.description: Where an ensemble produced the prediction, every member is listed with its name, version, and the probability it produced.
rules.rationale: An ensemble reported only by its aggregate is a single opinion wearing the authority of several. The member probabilities are what make disagreement, weighting, and exclusion visible at all.
rules.remediation: List every member that contributed, with the probability it produced.

rules.title: How members were combined is stated
rules.description: The record names the aggregation method that turned member probabilities into the reported one.
rules.rationale: A mean, a median, and a weighted mean give materially different answers from the same members, particularly when the members disagree. Without the method, the reported number cannot be reproduced from the parts.
rules.remediation: Record ensemble.aggregation.method, and the weights where they are not uniform.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator reads the method that was named. It does not recompute the aggregate from the members, because the space of legitimate aggregation schemes is wider than a checker can enumerate.

rules.title: Major disagreement among models is never ignored
rules.description: Where the spread between the highest and lowest member probability exceeds the project's threshold, the record declares the disagreement and says what it means for the prediction.
rules.rationale: Averaging two models that say 0.2 and 0.8 produces the same 0.5 as two models that both say 0.5, and the two situations warrant completely different confidence. Aggregation hides that distinction unless the spread is reported alongside it.
rules.remediation: Set ensemble.disagreement.declared with a note explaining the divergence, widen the interval, lower the confidence tier, or abstain citing model-disagreement.
rules.$assuranceNote: The spread is recomputed from the declared members, so this is exact for the models the record lists. It says nothing about models that were run and never mentioned.

rules.title: Models are not selected for producing the desired answer
rules.description: Every model excluded from the ensemble is listed with a reason that does not reduce to disagreeing with the result.
rules.rationale: Dropping the models that gave the wrong answer produces an ensemble that agrees with itself and with nothing else. Requiring the exclusions to be listed and reasoned makes the choice answerable instead of invisible.
rules.remediation: List each excluded model with a methodological reason, or include it and let the disagreement show.
rules.$assuranceNote: This can only see exclusions that were DISCLOSED. A model run and silently dropped leaves no trace in the record, so a pass here means the declared exclusions were reasoned, never that no cherry-picking occurred. Establishing that requires human review of how the ensemble was assembled.
